system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:46:31 UTC, the domain recorded creation of the account it_helper, with omar.haddad as the subject.
About two seconds later, it_helper was added to the Administrators group by the same subject and logon ID as the account creation event.
The account name and administrator membership conflict with the stated help-desk practice: temporary accounts use the tmp.<name> format and never receive administrator rights.

At 13:42:58 UTC, the domain recorded a Kerberos service-ticket event for omar.haddad targeting WS-BCARTER-01$, with source address 192.0.2.45. This is inconsistent with the stated remote-administration practice, which allows remote administration only from WS-OHADDAD-01.
The unexpected service-ticket event preceded creation of an account that was immediately made an administrator, supporting escalation as a likely malicious account-management event.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection on WS-BCARTER-01 was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, leaving a gap in endpoint process and authentication evidence during the relevant activity.
The available records do not include a corresponding domain logon event identifying the session represented by the subject logon ID on the account-change events.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish who controlled the source address 192.0.2.45 or whether it represents a specific person or device.
The evidence does not establish whether omar.haddad performed or authorized the changes, or whether the account was created using compromised credentials.
The evidence does not show what process or tool performed the account creation and group addition.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve domain-controller logon and directory audit records matching subject logon ID 0xfd8b8ad, including the authentication source and session details.
Investigate the origin and routing of 192.0.2.45 and correlate it with identity-provider, firewall, and endpoint records.
Recover any available WS-BCARTER-01 endpoint or centralized EDR telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC, and review WS-OHADDAD-01 for the expected remote-administration activity.
Confirm with omar.haddad whether the account creation and administrator-group addition were authorized, and check change records for approval.
Review the current state and subsequent activity of it_helper, including logons, group memberships, and changes made using the account.
